notes.text: Eventually always b — FG b in LTL. The machine guesses when the last a has gone by: "anything" loops on both symbols, and one nondeterministic b-edge commits to "only b", which has no a-transition at all. A wrong guess simply dies, which is exactly what nondeterminism is for.

This one cannot be made deterministic. Deterministic Büchi automata are strictly weaker than nondeterministic ones, and FG b is the standard witness — no DBA recognises it, because a deterministic run has to commit to "no more a's" without being able to see the rest of the infinite word.

meta.title: Classic: eventually always b
meta.blurb: FG b — from some point on, only b's. The textbook example of a language recognised by a nondeterministic Büchi automaton but by no deterministic one.
